beats.say: The Beatles recorded their entire debut album in just twelve hours.
After signing with EMI in May 1962, producer George Martin wanted a live album.
He visited the Cavern Club but found the venue was unsuitable for recording.
On 11 February 1963, the band arrived at EMI Studios to work fast.
They captured the raw energy of their live set in a single day.
Martin only added overdubs to two tracks, Misery and Baby It's You, later.
This marathon session created Please Please Me and changed music history forever.
